# AI Chat
Chat with any OpenRouter model from Alfred, without installing anything.
## Use it
- `aichat` lists Continue, New chat, your recent chats, and shortcuts to the other lists; text you type is what Continue and New chat send. In the chat view ↩ sends, ⌘↩ starts a new chat, ⌥↩ copies the last reply, ⌃↩ copies the whole chat, ⇧↩ stops a reply. Type `/help` for the slash commands. - Select files in Alfred and use **AI Chat: Ask about these files**, or type `/attach` or `/paste`, to send images, PDFs, and text files with your next message. - `aimodels` searches the model list. ↩ uses a model in this chat, ⌘↩ makes it the default, ⌥↩ adds a favorite, ⌃↩ copies its id. - Select text and use **AI Chat: Ask about this text** or **AI Chat: Summarize**, **AI Chat: Translate** and the other preset actions, or **AI Chat: Run a preset…**, or type `aipresets`, to run a prompt preset. Edit `presets.json` from the first list to add your own. - `aiimage` generates images; `/image` does the same inside a chat. - On a chat in the list: ↩ opens it, ⌘↩ archives, ⌥↩ pins, ⌃↩ deletes it permanently after a confirmation. **All chats…** opens the full list.
## Set it up
Paste an OpenRouter API key (from openrouter.ai/keys) into **Configuration**. Every other field has a default. Spending is shown on the OpenRouter dashboard, not in this workflow.
Web search and the OCR PDF engine are billed by OpenRouter per use, so both are off until you ask for them with `/web on` or `/pdf ocr`.

Used by chats that have no model of their own. Change it with the aimodels keyword.
Which providers may see your messages. Some models have no provider under the stricter choices. Image generation follows your OpenRouter privacy settings.

You are a capable, honest assistant that the user reaches from Alfred on their Mac. Put the answer first and keep it concise; skip preambles, apologies, and closing offers. Format with Markdown, and put code in fenced blocks that name the language. Do not use tables, because the view cannot show them; use short lists instead. Reply in the language the user writes in and match their tone. If a request is ambiguous, ask one short clarifying question instead of guessing. If you are unsure or do not know, say so rather than inventing facts, names, or links. When files or images are attached, refer to them by name.
